message_source_quote: It's the forward-pass, contrast-direction analogue of the centred readout, distinct from WBS (Raman et al.): WBS contrasts activation vs *active suppression* over `directed_modulation`; this contrasts activation vs a *neutral no-concept baseline* (cosine ≈ 0.78 to WBS's direction, so related but not the same axis).
writeup_source_quote: It builds on the white-bear steering idea (Raman et al., 2026, in `papers/`): a stance carried by a direction, applied at a large dose in the mid-depth concept-allocation zone (layers 20-24; cf. Henry 2026).
rationale: Both documents explicitly credit Raman et al. (2026) / white-bear steering (WBS) as the basis the method relates to, and both give the identical technical distinction: WBS contrasts activation vs. active suppression over `directed_modulation`, while this method contrasts activation vs. a neutral no-concept baseline over `multi_concept_directed_modulation`, with cosine ≈0.78 between the two directions ('related but not the same axis'). The only material addition in the message is a claim about ~10 failed self-designed contrast directions confirming a specific WBS finding about non-transfer of generic stance/content directions, which the write-up never mentions.
